sentence: This project studies how the Elongator complex controls small RNAs that help fission yeast cells form heterochromatin.
This project builds polymer nanodiscs that mimic lipoprotein particles in human blood to carry drugs for cancer treatment.
This project builds a handheld robotic device that collects plaque bacteria from the mouth and uses artificial intelligence to predict disease risk.
This project studies whether fluids coming from below the seafloor carry microorganisms from the deep biosphere up to the seafloor.
This project builds superconducting nanowire detector arrays that can measure extremely weak light, down to single photons.
This project studies how marine low clouds change as they move across the Pacific Ocean and how aerosols affect them.
This project studies understudied fungi and slime molds from local forests, using genome sequencing and chemical methods to look for natural products.
This project studies how plant cells control how much cellulose synthase reaches the plasma membrane, using live-cell imaging and proteomics.
This project builds methods that use data collected from cyber-physical systems to verify and control them without knowing their models.
This project studies how wind and sea ice affect how giant petrels use energy while foraging in the Southern Ocean.
This project builds a support system for a tool that turns machine learning models into digital hardware designs.
This project runs a programmable network that connects research facilities around the world so researchers can experiment with distributed systems.
This project studies how changes in gene regulation in different cell types help threespine stickleback fish adapt to marine and freshwater environments.
This project studies what rules decide which compounds a bacterial capsule polymerase can use to make different polysaccharide structures.
This project studies how wire arc additive manufacturing of molybdenum alloys causes residual stresses and pores and how they affect performance at high temperatures.
This project uses time-of-flight secondary ion mass spectrometry to study chemical processes at interfaces inside all-solid-state batteries during battery cycling.
This project studies the tools used to create AI abuse material and develops ways to make them harder to access and use.
